cards.claim: Frances Marie Burke won the 14th annual Miss America competition.
cards.quote: It was a chilly winter evening in February 1940 when the lights of the Warner Theatre in Atlantic City, New Jersey, shone bright, illuminating the stage for the 14th annual Miss America competition. Among the 42 contestants vying for the coveted title was a stunning 20-year-old from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania - Frances Marie Burke. Little did anyone know that this poised and charming young woman would soon make history, etching her name in the annals of American pageantry. Frances, a model by profession, had already gained recognition in the fashion world, gracing the covers of prominent magazines and strutting down catwalks with ease. Her experience in the industry had honed her confidence, and she was determined to bring home the Miss America crown. As the competition unfolded, Frances impressed the judges with her striking features, captivating stage presence, and impressive talent - a flawless rendition of the opera song "Caro Nome" from Verdi's Rigoletto. Her poise and elegance during the evening gown segment left the audience in awe, and her thoughtful responses to the judges' questions showcased her intelligence and wit. On February 10, 1940, the moment of truth arrived. The emcee, Bob Russell, announced the top five finalists, and Frances Marie Burke's name was among them. The tension was palpable as the judges deliberated, and finally, the results were in. With a beaming smile, Bob Russell declared, "And the new Miss America is... Frances Marie Burke!" The audience erupted in applause as Frances, resplendent in her evening gown, was crowned by the outgoing titleholder, Patricia Donnelly.

raw_card.claim: American model Frances Marie Burke was crowned the winner of the Miss Cyprus beauty contest.
